acceptanceCriteria: A proposed spec amendment defines tsconfig/jsconfig discovery, baseUrl/paths/extends resolution, extension and index inference, type-only edge strength, UNKNOWN for unresolved bare specifiers, and bounds (extends depth, config size), with numbered requirements and rollback.
On a fixture with baseUrl and wildcard paths, impact on a page object lists every spec importing it through an alias; a regression test fails without the change.
An import resolved only through an extends chain resolves; a cyclic or over-deep extends chain refuses or reports UNKNOWN, never guesses.
An `import type` edge is reported as type-only; an unresolved non-package bare specifier makes the impact result incomplete (UNKNOWN), never silently complete.
Index build and impact on a large TS repository stay ms-scale per query; config parsing is bounded and cached per index build.
body: Owner request https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/659 (2026-10-07). `corvint impact` on a TypeScript page object in an E2E repository finds only relative-import dependants; about 28 specs importing it through tsconfig baseUrl/paths (`import X from 'lib/pages/...'`) are missed, so test selection from a page-object or helper change is empty instead of failing closed, and the application map (issue 657) cannot reuse the import graph. Ask: resolve module specifiers through the nearest tsconfig.json/jsconfig.json (compilerOptions.baseUrl, paths with * wildcards, extends chains), index files and extension inference (.ts/.tsx/.d.ts) per TypeScript bundler/node resolution; report `import type` as a weaker edge; report unresolved bare specifiers as UNKNOWN rather than silently dropping them. Related: V1-0283 (workspace-package importers).
